text:
sam yang: hey team :wave: quick q — I need to spend ~3 months in Anchorage to care for my mom (late May to late Aug). wondering: can I temporarily change my homebase to AK for that period? how does that affect the WFH stipend, payroll withholding, and benefits eligibility?

Dana (People Ops): thanks for flagging, Sam. short answer: we can support a temporary satellite homebase but there are a few steps. main items: payroll/state tax withholding, benefits residency rules, and stipend proration/shipping.

sam yang: ok, what are the steps? I don’t want a long-term tax nexus for the company. :grimacing:

Dana (People Ops): 1) submit the "temporary homebase" form (link in #people-ops pinned). 2) notify payroll (lina) so they can review withholding changes. 3) we’ll check if AK creates a nexus (unlikely for a 3-month stay, but legal needs to confirm). 4) WFH stipend is prorated for partial months by default.

lina (Payroll): @sam we’ll need your projected dates and whether you’ll keep the same mailing address for pay documents. Alaska has no state income tax, so withholding likely stays at federal level only, but other things (unemployment state contributions) might be impacted. email payroll@redwood.com and put me on cc.

sam yang: got it — projected dates: 2026-05-20 to 2026-08-25. mailing address will be my parents' place in Anchorage.

Dana (People Ops): perfect. stipend note: WFH monthly stipend is paid pro rata if you don’t occupy that homebase for the full month. since your start date hits mid-May, May will be prorated. Also, shipping for equipment to Alaska is usually covered if requested in advance (submit a shipping request).

mike (Legal): tagging legal — long stays can sometimes create employer obligations in a state. AK typically low risk for short-term, but to be safe we’ll confirm. two quick asks: confirm you won’t be doing in-person customer work in AK, and confirm you won’t set up a vendor or office.

sam yang: I won’t be meeting customers in person, and no vendors/offices. it’s strictly caregiving + remote work.

andrew (Manager): backing this — also check connectivity (latency matters for our build hangs). if you need alternate hours we can flex. :+1:

Dana (People Ops): next steps for Sam: 1) fill the temporary homebase form 2) email payroll as Lina requested with dates + address 3) @mike we’ll hand off for legal confirm 4) shipping request if you need a spare monitor/desk items. I’ll follow up in 24–48h.

hr-bot: reminder — employees must not exceed 6 months continuous time in an alternate homebase without a formal relocation. This stay (3 months) is within policy. See policy: /policies/homebase-remote.md

lina (Payroll): copying the checklist I’ll need in the payroll email: full dates, physical address, payroll mailing address preference, tax-filing state if different, and whether you’ll be paid via direct deposit or need a temporary check.

sam yang: thanks all — I’ll submit the form today and loop Lina. appreciate the quick help. :relieved:
